docs.dcterms_abstract:
Printed in Cary's Memorials of the Civil War, Lond. 1842, vol. 2, p.306. 
 Concerning payment to her of a bill of £100 and another £100 to be
paid her by Mr. Will Crofts who was his master's ambassador in
Poland and certainly has all the King's money that he received there;
and concerning the safe transmission of the money to her, on which
he has several points. As to the news he gives a very favourable
opinion of the Scots army and good order of the forces under the
King's command. He bids her not to believe accounts of it put about
by the enemy in Fife. He describes the solemn proclamation of His
Majesty as King of England amid great acclamation as soon as we came
into England (see also his letter f.139) and again at Penrith.
"Those that are unwilling to hazard all in this cause with their
King have left us. This is a natural purge which will do as much
good".
